Subject: MAP: Load/perf test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - ExampleCorp

Hi Alicia / Platform team —

Thanks again for the great discovery call earlier. Per our conversation I attached a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_draft_ExampleCorp_v1.docx) with the milestones we discussed. The immediate MAP milestone we want to lock in is the load/performance test so Redwood and ExampleCorp can align on dedicated capacity sizing and any routing fallbacks.

Proposed milestone details (for the MAP):
- Milestone: Traffic replay / load test window
- Target window: Aug 24–Aug 25, 2026 (two 3-hour windows). Please confirm availability
- Goal: Validate peak QPS and 95th/99th percentile tail latency for prod-like traffic
- Deliverables: traffic_replay_manifest.txt + replay artifacts (S3 link), Redwood runbook, test report
- Owner: ExampleCorp to provide replay artifacts; Redwood SE (Vivek) to run test and size Dedicated nodes
- Dependencies: access to representative traffic, expected peak QPS, any IP allowlist for traffic replay agents
- Target close date for this MAP line item: 2026-09-03

Next steps I propose:
1) Alicia, can you confirm the replay artifacts availability and a rough peak QPS number?
2) Vivek, can you propose node sizing based on their QPS once confirmed?
3) I will send a calendar invite for the first window once we confirm times.

I've attached the MAP draft and a short load-test-plan for reference. Alicia — if you want, we can adjust window dates; we picked the 24–25th to give the procurement and infra teams time.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side:

- We can make a replay artifacts bundle available by Aug 20. I'll coordinate with our SREs to upload an S3 tarball.
- Our expected peak QPS (based on last quarter peak) is ~1,800 QPS sustained for ~10 minutes with traffic bursts up to 3,500 QPS for 30s.
- The proposed 24–25 windows look okay; prefer Aug 24 10:00–13:00 PT for the first window.
- Question: how many dedicated GPUs/nodes would Redwood expect to reserve to hit the 3,500 burst without queuing? Also, do you need any specific headers or auth tokens in the replay?

I'll loop in our Platform inbox for the S3 details (platform@examplecorp.com).

— Alicia

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Load/perf test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - ExampleCorp

Hi all — technical notes from the SE side after reviewing the expected profile: thanks for the QPS numbers, Alicia, that's very helpful.

Initial sizing recommendation (estimate):
- For sustained 1,800 QPS with 3,500 burst, I'd recommend a dedicated pool of 4 inference nodes (each 8xA100-equivalent) with burst autoscaling to add 2 nodes for short bursts. That should keep p95 latency within your SLA targets.
- If you want more headroom for concurrent context-heavy requests (long sequences, large prompt sizes), consider 6 nodes baseline.

Test requirements / playback notes:
- We will need a signed S3 URL for the replay bundle and an example request header set. Please ensure any PII is redacted in the bundle or provide instructions.
- Replay will run using Redwood's traffic-replay tool; we'll generate a test report with throughput, latency (p50/p95/p99), and token-level breakdowns.
- We'd like an initial dry-run at low QPS (~200) to validate the replay harness ~24 hours before the main window.

I'll prepare a sizing doc and attach a short runbook before the dry-run. Marissa — I can own the test execution and the node sizing recommendation milestone.

Cheers,
Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
